questions.prompt: A proposal for Access-path matrix measures 201/s and reserves 28% for failure, recovery, or skew. It plans steady demand at 132.7/s with a lower-priority shed point below the reserve. Should it ship? Name the deciding number and reversal evidence.

questions.prompt: A proposal for Page-capacity derivation measures 235/s and reserves 28% for failure, recovery, or skew. It plans 164.2/s steady demand, but only if a named fallback is active during recovery. Should it ship? Name the deciding number and reversal evidence.
questions.correct_answer: Approve conditionally for Page-capacity derivation. The deciding number is 235 x 0.72 = 169.2/s, and 164.2/s fits only while the fallback remains enforceable. Keep the condition until recovery traffic, priority demand, or fallback tests show less than 5/s of usable margin.

questions.prompt: A proposal for B+ tree split trace measures 269/s and reserves 28% for failure, recovery, or skew. It plans steady demand at 209.3/s and has no specific shed rule. Should it ship? Name the deciding number and reversal evidence.
questions.correct_answer: Decline B+ tree split trace at 209.3/s. The deciding number is 269 x 0.72 = 193.7/s, so planned demand exceeds the usable region by 15.6/s. Lift the decline if repeated measurements lift usable capacity above 209.3/s or a named policy removes at least 15.6/s of deferrable work before saturation.
